meta.what: Spec of the generated fix report: one self-contained, shareable HTML file per run, for a reviewer who decides Approve / Request changes / Reject.
meta.honesty: Only the bug-17 inputs are real files. Everything labelled illustrative has no artifact behind it. No verifier, judge, locate tool, fix-loop or report generator exists.
meta.sampleSource: analysis/explainer-src/62-report.html reads this file via window.ARGUS.report

principles: One file, no network, no CDN, no fonts: works from disk, from an Actions artifact, or attached to a PR.
Every number has a source field; a missing source renders "-", never a default.
Status is never colour alone: each state has a word and an icon.
Not run is not pass: overall status is pass_with_gaps when anything was skipped.
Untrusted text (ticket, rationale) goes in through textContent; the file ships with a script-src hash CSP.
Print-friendly: decision bar becomes a static block, all collapsed panels expand.

differsFromPlan.note: Owner flow: the owner types the issue (text or screenshot) in a console and gets this report. PLAN.md route: a labelled GitHub issue starts a durable workflow (P6-T07, P8-T08). The report is the same file either way; only ticket.source differs.

Owner flow: the PR is raised after Approve. Plan: a draft PR is opened first (find-or-create on one stable branch, draft until QA), and the QA signal marks it ready. In this report Approve therefore means "mark the draft ready", unless the owner decides to delay PR creation.

The decision bar needs somewhere to send the decision. A static HTML file opened from disk has none, so it falls back to copyable commands (gh pr ready <n>). The plan's endpoint is the P6 QA signal: MRTR input_required or a review comment with an approve keyword.
"Production UI" cannot mean the deployed site: data-src exists only in dev/test builds and the platform target is the synthetic copa-local cell.

ticket.text:
Text smaller than 12 px in many places (Radar, Horizon, Flights, Control Tower, admin tags).

On a phone at arm's length, 10 to 11 px text is hard to read. Counted per screen: Radar about 20 elements (labels such as INBOUND · LAST 24 H at 11 px, the CANCELLED tag at 10 px, scale labels at 10 px). Radar detail cards show CRITICAL, GROUND TIME, MINIMUM and DEPARTURE DELAY at 10 px. Horizon has Act now and Keep an eye at 11.5 px. The Flights list uses 11 px for crew position and status. Control Tower rules cells are 11 px. Admin tags (Read-only, Active, Intact, Failed, shadow) are 11.5 px.

Font sizes are set per component, with no minimum. Set a floor of 12 px for any text. No visible text under 12 px on any screen. Admin tags are 12 px or more.

The patches in this task cover apps/canvas/src/ops/radar.css only. Horizon, Flights, Control Tower and the admin tags are the same bug and are not in these diffs yet.
